result.title: Geo2Gcode: From 3D Geometry to CNC Programs through Structured Machining Primitives
result.summary: Turning a 3D shape into a Computer Numerical Control (CNC) program is still largely manual. For every part, a machinist chooses setups, tools, step-downs, and toolpath patterns. We present Geo2Gcode, which converts a target mesh directly into standard G-code through structured machining primitives. Each primitive couples an indexed machining direction, a closed per-view reconstruction of the target, and explicit tool-radius, layer-height, and clearing-pattern parameters, and compiles deterministically into layerwise toolpaths via signed-distance queries. Most of the fidelity comes from this compiler. A lightweight selector trained with a voxel stock simulator fills in primitive parameters without per-part manual settings, approaching the finest fixed setting at about a quarter of its toolpath length. In simulation on ABC parts, Geo2Gcode reaches roughing fidelity comparable to an expert-tuned commercial CAM setup with a moderately longer toolpath, and clearly improves on a default CAM configuration. Generated programs run in a commercial G-code simulator, and one part is machined on a physical CNC mill. These results demonstrate that roughing programs can be generated directly from geometry without per-part CAM tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文将目标三维网格直接编译为 CNC 加工程序：每个加工基元绑定加工方向、逐视角闭合重建与刀具半径、层高、清削模式等显式参数，并确定性地编译为分层刀路，再由在体素毛坯模拟器中训练的轻量选择器自动填充参数。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属制造几何领域，但“学习型轻量选择器提参数 + 确定性编译器保真”的分工，可能为 LVR 中 latent 提案与确定性解码之间的贡献分配、以及最小化学习组件职责的设计提供概念参照，需较多核查其可迁移性。
